page: Amazon Web Services c6g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the custom 64-bit ARM architecture AWS Graviton processor. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers 32 dedicated physical cores with 32 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz on ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. Each core features 64 KB L1 data cache and 1 MB L2 cache, supported by a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 64 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2 GB per core. The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps, does not contain local storage, and includes no dedicated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent multi-threaded processing characteristics paired with moderate single-core throughput. In synthetic CPU assessments, the instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core metric of 48574.31 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11649.0, sitting in the middle tier of tested hardware. Single-core results are comparatively modest, as reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 958.0 and single-threaded gzip compression performance of 20.33 GB/sec. Memory profiling shows 163.55 GB/sec read and 73.73 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks, though overall PassMark memory scoring remained in the lower quartile.

The 32 dedicated physical cores provide predictable thread isolation without hyperthreading contention, yielding strong efficiency for scale-out parallel workloads. Network-adjacent operational benchmarks show balanced execution, registering 38.64 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 33.12 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Software compilation in Geekbench via Clang scored 25603.0, further indicating solid multi-process scaling.

The primary operational tradeoff centers on single-threaded execution and reliance on network-attached storage, as no local NVMe drives are bundled. Workloads best aligned with the c6g.8xlarge include distributed web serving fleets, parallel code compilation pipelines, containerized microservices, batch processing, and horizontally scaled application runtimes adapted for arm64 execution.

The instance operates without local storage, relying on network-attached volumes, and delivers 12 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth without GPU accelerators. Performance metrics demonstrate competitive multi-threaded capacity, scoring 48574.31 in stress-ng multi-core and 11649.0 in Geekbench multi-core, offset by modest single-threaded metrics such as a 958.0 Geekbench single-core score. Cache provisions include 32 MB of L3 cache, supporting high-throughput parallel execution. This configuration represents an efficient resource allocation for multi-threaded workloads, CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed microservices, container clusters, and scalable web serving tiers.
